article.title: Why Customer Rank Thresholds Should Be Tested for Reachability, Not Just Distribution
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven business decisions.

paragraphs.en: A customer-tier threshold is often chosen from the spending distribution. Quartiles, deciles, or round monetary values can create neat groups, but a statistically tidy boundary is not necessarily a useful behavioral target. Suppose a four-tier program places the next threshold 100,000 yen above most customers in the second tier. The groups may be balanced, yet only a small fraction can realistically close the gap. Reachability asks how many customers have plausible behavioral headroom. Calculate the distance to the next threshold and translate it into familiar actions, such as extra monthly visits, additional basket value, or category expansion. The calculation should use realistic baselines. If normal annual spending is 60,000 yen, another 80,000 yen may be mathematically possible but behaviorally implausible. Distribution describes how customers are currently arranged; reachability describes whether the architecture creates credible pathways for movement. Analysts can compare candidate cutoffs and the share of customers within several distances of the next level. However, being close to a threshold does not mean a customer should automatically receive an incentive. Some will cross naturally; others may respond only to discounts that cost more than the incremental margin. Historical migration helps calibrate expectations, and experiments can test whether progress messages or benefits change movement. Inflation also matters because a spending threshold can become easier to reach when prices rise without real quantity growth. The best cutoff balances distribution, realistic headroom, benefit economics, simplicity, and the behavior the program intends to change. Before launch, teams can simulate how many customers would enter each tier, how many sit near an upgrade boundary, and how much additional spending or frequency would be required. They can compare several threshold sets rather than treating the first quartile solution as final. A useful design also considers stability: customers should not move between levels simply because small seasonal fluctuations change the cutoff. Fixed monetary thresholds can improve predictability, while periodic reviews can keep them economically relevant. Communication quality matters because customers must understand what action moves them upward. Reachability is therefore both an analytical and a product-design question. paragraphs.zh: Tier cutoff除了distribution也要測reachability，把差額轉成額外visit或basket，並結合自然升級、responsiveness、incremental margin與規則穩定性。
paragraphs.ja: Cutoffは人数比だけでなくreachability、realistic headroom、incremental margin、ruleの安定性まで評価します。
